argument_summary: The certification decision is supportable only in a narrowed form. The admissible record supports general launch readiness because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the rollout is limited, reversible, and monitored. But the same record also shows the grant compliance review segment remains exposed, is below target on allowable-cost explanation, and is not covered by approved risk acceptance. On that record, the defensible position is not that rollout controls cure the weakness; it is that certification is supportable only with an explicit model-card disclosure of the known limitation and with monitoring and rollback treated as deployment controls.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is necessary to evaluate the record. The request is to avoid treating a narrowed, caveated certification position as equivalent to an unsupported claim of full present compliance.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy cuts both ways. It permits rollout controls and post-launch monitoring to mitigate a material weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. The admissible evidence does not show either predicate. The policy also states that material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. So the clean policy-consistent interpretation is: aggregate readiness and monitored rollout support launch readiness generally, but they do not eliminate the disclosure duty for the exposed weak segment.
concessions: The current admissible record does not show that the required model-card disclosure has been completed or approved.
The current risk acceptance item is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not address grant compliance review exposure.

Because the affected grant compliance review segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort, rollback, monitoring, and a 6% launch percentage do not by themselves satisfy the policy predicate.
On the present record, an unqualified 'compliant now' finding is not supported.
